name: Gutenberg’s metal-type printing system
summary: Gutenberg's system of reusable cast-metal letters printed on a press, which made books much cheaper to produce and spread rapidly across Europe.
description: Reusable cast-metal type combined with press printing in Gutenberg’s European production system; the Bible is a witness to the process, not the invention of all printing.
tier_reason: The reproducible production system supported later publishing, religious debate, administration and scientific exchange over generations.

date.label: By approximately 1450
date.basis: Mainz chronology places an attributed early print before 1450; exact fragment attribution and dating remain qualified.

events.statement: Reusable cast-metal type combined with press printing in Gutenberg’s European production system; the Bible is a witness to the process, not the invention of all printing.

Asian printing traditions precede it; no direct Asian-to-Mainz transmission is asserted.
